It is submitted that the Gumsudgi report Ex.P/7 is a story which reveals the correct clever of the incident.
Later on, prosecutrix on some instructions, changed the story.

Prosecutrix, in her statement Ex.D/1, has 3 CRA-5486-2023 given a story that on 30/09/2020 at night about 2.00 a.m. her Bhabhi was going to watch dance of local community (Bedniyo) and when she also followed her, however, on the way she was abducted by four persons namely three of the appellants whose names have been mentioned above and one Dayaram Choudhary.
Thereafter allegation is that she was taken to a house where she was forced to consume liquor then these four persons violated her privacy.
Later on, she was taken on a motorcycle by Dayaram Choudhary and then he kept her for 10-15 days and continuously violated her privacy.

In Ex.P/7, it is mentioned that sister-in-law of the prosecutrix in the morning of 1st October, 2020 informed the father of the prosecutrix who is the author of missing person report Ex.P/7 that at about 6.00 a.m. prosecutrix left home without informing anybody.
It is also mentioned in Ex.P/7 that she had carried her Aadhar Card and her age is 18 years three months.
Reading from this missing person report, learned counsel for the appellants submit that in fact prosecutrix was in relationship with Dayaram Choudhary.

She wanted to marry him, therefore, she had taken her Aadhar Card, otherwise there was no occasion for her to carry her Aadhar Card to watch dance of Santosh Kumar Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179610439/

sentences.text: 2 the local community (Bedniyo).
It is submitted that report was lodged on 2nd October, 2020 whereas father of prosecutrix had returned back to the village from Bhopal where he had gone to work on 1st October, 2020 itself.

Thus, it is submitted that on account of old enmity and with a view to give colour under the Special Act, appellant-Santosh Kumar Patel has been falsely implicated whereas appellant-Balua Choudhary is the cousin brother of main accused -Dayaram Choudhary and Ganguram Choudhary is also related to 4 CRA-5486-2023 the main accused, therefore, they have been falsely implicated.

Our attention is drawn to the evidence of the concerned lady doctor P.W.3-Dr. Sunita Singh and reading from the evidence of P.W.3 and also the evidence of prosecutrix (P.W.1) in regard to appellants-Balua, Ganguram Choudhary and Santosh Kumar Patel, it is submitted that its a case of false implication qua them and even DNA report Ex.C/1 is positive qua only Dayaram Choudhary who has not referred any appeal till date.

It is interesting to note that prosecution did not deem it fit to examine sister-in- law of the prosecutrix with whom she narrated her case diary statement Ex.D/1 to have followed her to watch a community dance (Bedniyo).
It is submitted that case of Dayaram Choudhary, being different as his DNA has matched, therefore, he will not be entitled to claim any parity with the co- accused persons.

Shri Aditya Narayan Gupta, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail and submits that prosecutirx has given the complete version of the incident to the doctor P.W.3.

But, he is not in a position to explain that when prosecutrix was asked in her cross-examination that she had stayed with main accused- Dayaram Choudhary for over 10 days and that too in a shared household where there were several houses in the neighbourhood,
then why she had not informed any of the persons in the locality about the incident.
Plea of alibi taken by Ganguram could not be proved by examining any witness in the evidence.

Taking these facts into consideration and without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellants of both the above criminal appeals i.e. Bablua, Ganguram and Santosh Kumar Patel and release them on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.8624/2023 and I.A. No.10298/2023 are allowed.

It is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for their appearance before the Trial Court on 18.12.2024 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellants of both the above criminal appeal i.e. Balua,
Ganguram and Santosh Kumar Pate shall remain suspended and they be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
